steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart casserole dish.
Combine butter, whole corn, creamed corn, cornbread mix, and sour cream in a mixing bowl until combined.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown and set, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Cornbread Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This cornbread casserole recipe takes minutes to prepare with 5 easy ingredients: canned corn, creamed corn, sour cream, butter, and cornbread mix.
raw_recipe.name: Cornbread Casserole

recipeInstructions.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart casserole dish.
Combine butter, whole corn, creamed corn, cornbread mix, and sour cream in a mixing bowl until combined.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown and set, about 1 hour.

review.reviewBody: I've tried a few cornbread casserole recipes and this is by far the best! I love that there is no egg in it! I will never bother to try another corn casserole recipe again, this one was perfect! Just a note, you do have to drain the whole kernel corn.

I made this for a work potluck and it went over great. I gave the recipe out to a few. I did take the advice of others and added 8 oz sour cream, 2 eggs and I aded 1/3 cup of white sugar. The recipe didn't say whether or not to drain the corn and I did. Next time, I'll leave the juice in. I also dusted the buttered dish with a light coating of sugar. This dish was gone in a flash!
Thank you.

Great way to take ordinary corn bread and transform the traditional into something different, good and very tasty. My family loves this recipe. It's tried and true, I love the texture. I made one adjustment to it because when I cooked it for an hour it was still a little bit mushy so I kept cooking it for about 1 hour and 15 minute to an hour and a half. It was just right!
I love this recipe. I accidently left out the butter the last time I made this, but the taste is still the same! I'll be omitting the butter from now on when I make this.

1 stick of butter, melted 1 (15 ounce) can whole kernel corn, not drained 1 small can creamed corn 2 packages jiffy cornbread mix 8 ounces sour cream 2 eggs Directions Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). In a mixing bowl, combine butter, whole corn, cream corn, corn muffin mix and sour cream. Fold all ingredients together, pour into 2 quart casserole dish. Bake for 1 hour. I looked at a lot of recipes to try and figure out "Becky's" exact recipe. I am still unsure that this is the correct amounts, but I don't really think you can go wrong with these ingredients! This recipe says to cook it for 1 hour... I would check it at 45 minutes. Enjoy!

I LOVE this recipe! I printed it out last year and have made it at least 10 times since. I wouldn't change anything! The only thing I notice is that the recipe doesnt say to drain the can of regular corn. Oh, and it really does need about an hour to bake. but SO YUMMY! :)

I changed the recipe to suit my family.
I used two boxes of Jiffy cornbread mix
and added a cup of buttermilk. I also
peppered the batter.

I also greased the pan with bacon grease.

Very good. We like this with chili or 
warmed the next day with eggs and bacon.

Jazz this us up by cooking a pound of ground beef, place in bottom of pan, add a layer of cheddar cheese, add jalapeno's to according to your taste in cornbread mixture and pour over cheese. It is fantastic.

I thought this recipe was very good my family loves it. The recipe I have calls for 1 box of phildelphia cream cheese instead of sour cream.I simply melt butter and cream cheese in microwave for about 2-3 minutes or until soft. I am always asked to bring this dish for family get together and potlucks.

I was going for a cornbread that's like bread rather than casserole. 

I customized the recipe by adding another 8.5 oz. Jiffy cornbread mix (total of 2 boxes or 17 oz.). I used 1 15 oz. can whole kernal corn and 1 can of sweet kernel corn, NO Butter, NO sour cream, and 1 egg. I pre-heated at at 375 degrees and baked for about 30-35 minutes. I sprayed the 9x13 casserole dish with spray to prevent it from sticking. It turned out to be a moist cornbread and was a hit with my party of 9.

Delicious and so easy! I fried four pieces of bacon (cut in small pieces) and added that to the mixture, along with the bacon grease. I also added two eggs. It came out perfect, almost souffle like. I topped it with three green onions cut in fine slices, including the chives, it gave it a little crunch and added some nice color, as well. I didn't drain the whole kernel corn and baked in a lightly oiled preheated iron skillet. Will definitely make this again!
i made this recipe exactly as directed and it didn't turn out.

I doubled the batch and place them in 2 separate 2-quart casserole dishes. I cooked them at the same time. I did not have to have to change anything. My friend added tuna in it and Ritz crackers for the topping. Has anyone tried it with tuna in it and Ritz crackers for the topping.

I have a very similar recipe except I do this. Add 1 stick of melted butter, 1 cup sour cream, and 1 can of green chilis. If you want it hotter, dice up a jalapeno and add it. If you want it a little sweeter, add 1-2 tablespoons of sugar. Enjoy!
Easy and delicious. I have added cubed ham and cheese to the recipe. Be sure to cook the cubed ham in a frying pan fist to get the moisture out. Yum

I make this only better. I don’t use the sour cream and instead I put in 1-7ounce can of whole chilies, sliced open. I put half the batter into my 8”x 8” pyrex dish, lay the opened chilies on top, add the remaining batter. Then I top with grated cheddar. Try it❣️ I think you will like it even better.

I make it pretty much the same way, except I use 2-eggs beaten, I do not drain the whole kernel corn, and I use 8 oz. of sour cream or half of a 16 oz. carton. and i use 1/2 cup of margarine (1 stick). mix it up and bake the same and watch for the top to slightly brown.
I am no longer allowed to have a holiday meal without it. Today, I am making it for a friend, who is recovering from surgery. She specifically requested it.
